chapter: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
title: Standard Theater in Philadelphia with Jack Johnson and Ethel Waters
summary: He recalls the 1924 Standard Theater bill with Jack Johnson's exhibition boxing, Ethel Waters, the Berry Brothers and others, and other Philadelphia theatres.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, the places were outstanding. Steel Pier was outstanding, you know. Being on the Boardwalk in Atlantic City is outstanding where it was done and the year it was done in. And then we go to the Standard Theater in Philadelphia in 1924, had the privilege of playing with Jack Johnson on the program doing exhibition boxing. I guess you remember Jack Johnson, dontcha?
Our first heavyweight championship by a champion fighter, rather. Then on the program there at the Standard Theater, Ethel Waters on the bill and

Sandy Burns is the comedian, Marshall "Garbage" Rogers comedian, at the Standard Theater. Then we had the Berry Brothers. We had Ada Brown and Sam Russell who was a comedian, George Wilshire was a straight man and we had the Lucky Seven Trio, was a dancing trio. Then we played the Fox Theater in Philadelphia and played the Shubert Theater with Herman Timberg's (phonetic spelling) "Frolics of 1922." We played the Pearl Theater in Philadelphia and we played at the southwest Phillie, we played the Pearl and in West Philadelphia we played the Lancaster Theater called The William Penn on Lancaster Avenue in 1925 and it was an all-white show.
